prompt: You plan to film with 8 cameras. How many servers do you need?
feedback: Each server takes 2 cameras, so 8 cameras need 4 servers.

prompt: You book the cameras ahead of the event. When do the servers start?
options: 10 minutes early, so the cameras are ready on time
On the stroke of 07:00
30 minutes early
The evening before
feedback: A booking made ahead starts its servers 10 minutes early.

prompt: The head referee starts the cameras straight away. About how long until they are ready?
options: Under a minute
About 30 minutes
About an hour
About 5 minutes
feedback: Starting a booking straight away takes about 5 minutes.

prompt: The event runs over two days. What camera hours apply?
options: 07:00 to 18:00 on the first day only
07:00 to 18:00 local time on each day
08:00 to 20:00 on each day
Midnight to midnight on both days
feedback: The cameras run from 07:00 to 18:00, local time, on each day of the event.

prompt: Before the day, you check the venue's connection. What must it be able to do?
options: Carry the video from the busiest camera only
Run the AI judge on site
Carry the video from every camera at once, about 3.5 Mbit/s each
Give every phone its own separate network
feedback: Each camera sends about 3.5 Mbit/s, and the venue's connection has to carry all of them.

prompt: The head referee can't be reached and the cameras need stopping. Who else can stop any event's cameras?
options: An admin
Any referee assigned to the event
Any referee at the race
The owner of each camera phone
feedback: Admins can book, extend or stop any event's cameras.

prompt: A volunteer brings an Android phone to use as a camera. Which app does it need?
options: Larix Broadcaster
The phone's own camera app
A web browser
SpartanReferee Broadcaster
feedback: Android phones use the SpartanReferee Broadcaster app. Larix is for iPhones.

prompt: Why does each camera phone need a power bank?
options: To boost its signal to the server
To keep it going all day
To run the AI judge on the phone
To let it film without any connection
feedback: Each camera needs a power bank to keep the phone going all day.

prompt: Where does a referee find an event's camera hours and who is refereeing it?
options: By opening the event from their home page
On the Live tab of a camera
In the Larix app
On a camera's QR code
feedback: Your events are on your home page. Open one to see its camera hours and who is refereeing it.

prompt: A referee on the event wants to watch the cameras on their own laptop. What should they do?
options: Install Larix Broadcaster
Install SpartanReferee Broadcaster
Open it in a browser: there is nothing to install
Ask for a second server for the laptop
feedback: Any phone, tablet or computer with a browser will do, with nothing to install.

prompt: A phone on its stand 1 metre from the lane cuts off the athletes' legs. What is the fix?
options: Move it even closer
Pick a lower quality
Switch the picture to portrait
Move it back to about 3 to 4 metres
feedback: Place the phone 3 to 4 metres from the athletes, with each athlete's whole body in the picture.

prompt: How should a camera phone sit on its stand?
options: In landscape
In portrait
Either way: the server rotates it
Tilted at 45 degrees
feedback: Put the phone in landscape on its stand.

prompt: You are framing the shot. What must stay in the picture?
options: Just the athlete's chest and hands
Each athlete's whole body, including when they lie flat
Only the athlete's legs and feet
Only the athlete while standing
feedback: Keep each athlete's whole body in the picture, including when they lie flat on the ground.

prompt: The judge struggles to see chest to the ground from a camera straight on. What helps?
options: Moving the phone back to 10 metres
Picking a lower quality
A slightly angled or side-on view
Putting an official in front of the phone
feedback: A slightly angled or side-on view judges chest to the ground better than straight on.

prompt: How does the judge treat an official in a hi-vis yellow top?
options: It counts them if they stand in front of the camera
It never counts them as an athlete
It counts them only if they do a burpee
It counts them but marks them separately
feedback: Officials in hi-vis yellow tops are never counted as athletes.

prompt: Where does a camera that is waiting for its phone show its QR codes?
options: On the Results tab
On the Watch page only
In the Larix app
On the Live and Cameras tabs
feedback: Each waiting camera shows QR codes on the Live and Cameras tabs of the console.

prompt: Why must you scan a camera's QR code again for each new booking?
options: The codes change with every booking
The phone forgets its apps after a day
The server keeps one code per phone for ever
Larix deletes imported cameras after use
feedback: The codes change with every booking, so scan them again each time.

prompt: An Android phone is ready to connect. What quality do you leave it on?
options: The lowest setting, to save power
The highest setting, for the best picture
720p, unless the signal is weak
480p, unless the signal is strong
feedback: Leave the quality on 720p unless the signal is weak.

prompt: You have just installed Larix Broadcaster on an iPhone. What do you do before scanning the code?
options: Open it once, allowing the camera and microphone
Restart the phone
Press the red button
Switch on aeroplane mode
feedback: Install Larix and open it once, allowing the camera and microphone.

prompt: On an iPhone, how do you get the camera into Larix?
options: Scan the code from inside Larix's camera view
Scan the Android code with Larix
Type the camera's name into Larix
Scan the iPhone (Larix) code with the phone's own camera, open the link in Larix and tap Import
feedback: Scan the iPhone code with the phone's own camera, open the link in Larix and tap Import.

prompt: You have pressed Start AI judge, named the camera and chosen the exercise. What is the last step?
options: Scan the QR code again
Press Start judging
Open the Results tab
Wait for the head referee to approve it
feedback: After naming the camera and choosing what it judges, press Start judging.

prompt: A burpee has full hip extension and hands over the ears, but both feet stay on the ground. What is it?
options: A good rep, as most checks passed
A good rep if the athlete lands cleanly
A half rep that counts for half
A no rep, because it missed the jump
feedback: A burpee needs a jump with both feet off the ground. A rep that misses one check is a no rep.

prompt: What does the judge look for in the jump on a burpee?
options: Both feet off the ground
One foot off the ground
Hands clapping overhead
A jump forward past the starting line
feedback: The judge checks for a jump with both feet off the ground.

prompt: When should you do test reps in front of a camera?
options: After the first wave has finished
At the first camera only
Before athletes arrive, at every camera
Only if a camera drops
feedback: Do a few test reps in front of each camera before athletes arrive.

prompt: During a test rep the athlete steps out of the picture. What do you do?
options: Restart the AI judge
Move the phone
Switch the phone to mobile data
Pick a lower quality
feedback: If an athlete leaves the picture, move the phone.

prompt: An athlete says the judge got a rep wrong. How do you see exactly what happened?
options: Scroll back on the Live tab
Start the AI judge again on that camera
Use Watch to play them back with every rep and no rep marked
Ask the head referee to book the cameras again
feedback: Watch plays the athlete back with every rep and every no rep marked.

prompt: It is two days after the event. Can referees still review the results?
options: No: they are deleted when the booking ends
Yes: recordings and results are kept for 7 days
Only the head referee can, for 24 hours
Only admins can
feedback: Recordings and results are kept for 7 days, and every referee on the event can review them.

prompt: A phone will not connect to its camera. What do you try?
options: Book another server
Pick a lower quality
Restart the AI judge
Check its signal and scan its code again from this booking
feedback: If a phone won't connect, check its signal and scan its code again from this booking.

prompt: A camera's picture keeps stuttering and dropping. What does that point to?
options: The signal is too weak for 720p, so pick a lower quality
The venue is blocking video, so use mobile data
No server is free, so try again later
The phone is in the wrong orientation
feedback: A stuttering or dropping picture means the signal is too weak for 720p. Pick a lower quality.

prompt: You booked the cameras but a server did not start. What do you do?
options: Scan every QR code again
Switch every phone to Larix
Read what the console says; if no server is free, try again in a few minutes
Pick a lower quality on each phone
feedback: The console says why. Sometimes there is no server free for a few minutes, so try again.

prompt: Where does the AI judge run when you use the free camera?
options: On a SpartanReferee server
On a practice server
In the Larix app
In your own browser
feedback: The free camera runs the AI judge in your own browser.

prompt: What does using the free camera cost?
options: A 30-minute booking each time
Nothing: there is no server and no cost
The cost of one server
A booking by a head referee
feedback: The free camera needs no server and has no cost.

prompt: When can you use the free camera?
options: At any time
Only during an event's camera hours
Only after a head referee books it
Only in a 30-minute slot
feedback: You can use the free camera at any time.

prompt: Who can book a 30-minute practice server?
options: Any referee
Anyone with a browser
Head referees and admins
Only the race director
feedback: A practice server is for head referees and admins.

prompt: How long is a practice server booking?
options: 10 minutes
30 minutes
1 hour
A full event day
feedback: A practice server is booked for 30 minutes.

prompt: Why are practice servers limited to head referees and admins?
options: They cost referees money
They need an app only head referees can install
Only head referees have a review page
A practice server uses one of the servers events need
feedback: It uses one of the servers events need, so it is for head referees and admins.

prompt: You have a laptop and a minute of video of someone doing burpees. How can you see them judged?
options: With a practice server only
By booking an event's cameras
With the free camera, which can judge a minute of video
With Larix Broadcaster on its own
feedback: The free camera judges your own device's camera, live or on a minute of video.

prompt: A head referee wants to rehearse the phones, the console, the judge and the review before an event. What should they book?
options: A 30-minute practice server
Another event booking
Nothing: the free camera does all of it
An extra server on the event day
feedback: A practice server rehearses the whole station, just as at an event.

prompt: Which of these can only be rehearsed on a practice server, not the free camera?
options: Watching a burpee being judged
Phones scanning their codes to connect
Using your own device's camera
Using it at any time
feedback: The practice server rehearses the phones scanning their codes, as at an event. The free camera uses your own device.

prompt: How do you try the free camera with your own phone?
options: Book a server first
Scan a QR code with Larix
Ask the head referee for a booking
Prop the phone up, do a few burpees and watch each one judged
feedback: Prop the phone up, do a few burpees and see each one judged.
